options: Resources are acquired lazily on first use and only released when the program exits
A resource is acquired in a constructor and released in the destructor of its owning object
Every resource is allocated on the heap and reclaimed later by a tracing garbage collector
The programmer must call release() explicitly in a finally block on every exit path
questions.explanation: RAII binds a resource to an object's lifetime; destructors run on every exit path including exceptions.

questions.prompt: A 50 Hz loop runs for 2 minutes and leaks a 128-double buffer on every cycle. How many bytes leak in total? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: 50 x 120 = 6000 cycles; 128 x 8 = 1024 bytes each: 6,144,000 bytes.

questions.prompt: A class owns a double* released in its destructor and has no other special members. What happens in 'Scan b = a;' when both go out of scope?
options: Both destructors free the same memory: a double free
The copy allocates fresh storage automatically
Only the first destructor frees; the second is skipped
questions.explanation: The implicit copy constructor copies the pointer value, so two objects own one block.

questions.prompt: What does std::move(x) do by itself?
options: It destroys x and leaves the name x referring to deallocated storage
It casts x to an rvalue reference so a move overload can be chosen
It copies x and marks that copy as a temporary that can be stolen from
It immediately transfers x's resources into a newly created destination object
questions.explanation: std::move is only a cast; the move constructor or assignment that is then selected does the transfer.

questions.prompt: Four cameras each deliver a 2.5 MB frame at 20 Hz. If every frame is deep-copied once, how many MB per second are copied? Give a number.
questions.explanation: 4 x 2.5 MB x 20 = 200 MB/s of copy traffic; a move would be O(1) per frame.

questions.prompt: A copyable type has a move constructor that is not marked noexcept. What does std::vector do when it grows?
options: It reuses the old storage in place without relocating any element
It refuses to compile until the move constructor is marked noexcept
It copies the elements to keep the strong exception guarantee
It moves them anyway and terminates if one of the moves throws
questions.explanation: std::move_if_noexcept selects the copy when the move may throw and a copy exists.

questions.prompt: A subscriber callback receives a camera frame. Choose parameter types for (a) rendering the frame immediately, and (b) queueing it for a worker thread that may run after the callback returns. Justify each in terms of ownership and lifetime.
rubric: (a) const Frame& (borrow): the caller keeps ownership and the frame outlives the call.
(b) Needs ownership or shared lifetime: unique_ptr moved in, or shared_ptr<const Frame>; a reference or raw pointer would dangle.
Mentions the cost trade-off: no copy of a large frame versus unbounded queue or reference counting overhead.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
